title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: November 4 | Week 9 vs. Seattle Seahawks
headline: With Jeremiyah Love on IR and Bam Knight out of practice, Tyler Allgeier is the lead back for Seattle. Michael Wilson (ribs) is limited but improving.
summary: LaFleur declined to say much about a trade involving a locker-room leader, only that the team is letting the process play out and that it should be finalized in the next few days. He confirmed the Wednesday injury report: Bam Knight, Jon Gaines and Jayden Williams are out, Isaiah Adams and Michael Wilson are limited, and Reggie Virgil is full. Budda Baker, Hjalte Froholdt and Isaac Seumalo got rest days. He praised Tyler Allgeier, the NFC Player of the Week, and said he told him on Wednesday of last week that he would have a big third-down role while Love and Bam split early downs. Allgeier ended up carrying the load as the only healthy back. Love is on IR and disappointed, and Bam's status is unknown. James Conner will not play this week, and LaFleur is taking him week to week. He spoke warmly of Gardner Minshew's work ethic and calm in big moments and said the offense is built to fit what its players do well. He called Seattle arguably the best defense in football, in a hostile environment, and said Arizona's defense is trending the right way. He gave no commitment on adding another quarterback or on how the backfield will look once Bam returns.

title: Kevin Stefanski on Atlanta Falcons arrival in Madrid, Spain | Press Conference
headline: Stefanski gave no snap count for a player he called 'James' (not a roster name) who hasn't practiced in a month, while Bijan Robinson got heavy praise ahead of the Bengals game in Madrid.
summary: Stefanski spoke right after the Falcons landed in Madrid, mostly about the trip, the host setup at Real Madrid's facility, and the challenge of facing Cincinnati. He said the team wants to get 'back to who we are' on offense after a tough loss last week, but he gave no scheme or personnel details. Wednesday's session was only a mobility circuit and walkthrough, with full-speed practices set for Thursday and Friday. Asked about snaps for a returning player the captions render as 'James', he said the player has been with the team for a month without practicing but has trained in the weight room. The plan will be set after this week's practices and he had no exact snap number. He called Bijan Robinson a rare mix of speed, power and agility, a home-run threat who can also get hard yards. He said he sees Michael Penix Jr. growing as a player and leader in his first year working with him. He praised Cincinnati's offense, singling out Joe Burrow and two elite receiving playmakers, and said it can beat both light and eight-man boxes.

title: Dave Canales discusses how the defense has responded after making a change at DC
headline: Panthers made a defensive coaching change midseason, with Todd taking on a larger coordinator role. Canales said nothing on offensive players or injuries in this clip.
summary: Canales opened by praising the team's response at the first practice after an emotional few days, citing energy, urgency, and a push to stack consistency. He said the group has to rally together to find solutions, starting in the classroom and carrying over to the field. Asked about a bigger linebacker role for Darren Bates after a coach (transcribed as "Mayor") left the organization, he said no. AC is now coaching the whole front, including the outside linebackers and defensive tackles, so that Todd can focus on his job as coordinator. Pete still coaches the linebackers, and Darren helps in that room. He declined to detail the decision to move on from Mayor, calling it a personal matter between the two of them, though he spoke respectfully of him. He pushed back on a reporter's suggestion that the move was related to EJ and Cooley. He praised Todd's first impression, saying he coached the D line with a lot of energy and kept players focused on the present. The transcript cuts off as a reporter asks about a possible move to a 4-3 defense.

title: Ben Johnson on passing game clicking | Press Conference
headline: Bears' passing game is distributing targets more cleanly (Rome, Luther, Colston all rotating hot), while D'Andre Swift's heavy workload is being monitored and the run game remains inconsistent ahead of a tough Tampa run defense/offense matchup.
summary: Johnson opened by praising the Buccaneers as a hot team, winners of three of four, with the league's top rushing attack and a defense playing at a high level. He said the Bears' passing game has gotten cleaner, with Caleb Williams completing a high rate and spreading the ball to all his pass catchers after early-season lulls. He described target volume as cyclical, noting Luther Burden III started a recent game hot, Colston Loveland carried the middle stretch, and Rome Odunze came on late, and said it is hard to feed everyone as they deserve. He called the run game inconsistent and spotty, with first-half rushing lagging second-half rushing, but said the line and tight ends are blocking well and a breakthrough is coming. Swift averaged under three yards per carry last week but is praised for vision and finishing near the goal line, and Johnson said the staff is conscious of his carry volume and monitors it during games. Red-zone efficiency has risen after ranking 32nd. On injuries, Kentavius Street was confirmed done for the year, and Johnson was noncommittal on the status of others, saying a few players will need to be watched through the week. He also said a bye is coming soon, and praised Caleb's preparation and growing confidence and speed.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: November 4th, 2026
headline: Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol but is expected to practice with the ones today. His Sunday status at New Orleans is open, and Shedeur Sanders is being prepared as a real possibility to start.
summary: Monken said Watson felt fine after the game but developed a headache Monday night and self-reported Tuesday, so he is in the concussion protocol. He is expected to take first-team reps today, and Monken would not rule him out for Sunday. He said the protocol is harder for a quarterback than it was for Tytus Howard last week, because a quarterback needs practice reps to build timing with receivers. Monken is excited to see Shedeur Sanders work with the ones today. He pointed to Sanders' heavy camp reps, his full participation in meetings and film, and the extra walkthroughs and meetings coming this week. The team game-planned for the chance that Sanders starts, and Monken does not expect the offense to change dramatically. He said Watson is still the starter when healthy. Austin Barber, Maliek Collins and a player the captions render as "Quincy" are all considered not out, and Monken is optimistic about them without ranking their chances. He defended rookie left tackle Spencer Fano after a rough game in Pittsburgh, and he blamed the team's slow starts on turnovers, penalties and early run defense.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “It’s Not an Effort Issue, It’s an Execution Issue” | Press Conference
headline: Cowboys plan to get George Pickens more involved early and via motion; Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke remain in concussion protocol, Malachi Lawrence out a few weeks, and Jake Ferguson is only working with trainers.

Locke, are still in the concussion protocol, and edge rusher Malachi Lawrence is expected to miss a few weeks. He said Pickens is a priority, he is banged up but playing through it, and the plan is to move him around and get him going earlier, with the responsibility falling on him as play caller. He pushed back on any target-quota idea, saying the ball gets spread around when you have both Pickens and CeeDee Lamb having good years. He explained the drop in pre-snap motion as a result of playing from behind in a couple of games, and said big plays are being hurt by pass-interference penalties that do not show up in the stat book. His message to the team after the overtime loss to Arizona was about consistency and execution, not effort: the defense was good for three quarters but the offense failed to close the game out late. He defended wanting a balanced offense and called Dak Prescott an MVP-caliber player. On defense he cited problems covering flat routes and handling tempo, and said the team is most comfortable in nickel. He also said the offensive line has been inconsistent in pass protection and the run game.

title: HC Sean Payton on Broncos facing Panthers: ‘It’s an explosive team’
headline: Payton denies any J.K. Dobbins load-management concern and says the backfield rotation stays hot-hand, while rookie Jonah Coleman earned praise as a third-down and pass-catching back.
summary: Payton opened Week 9 prep for the Panthers by calling them an explosive team, about seventh or eighth in explosive plays, that mixes play-action and RPOs and has drafted well. He said Carolina's recent coordinator change leaves little to scout beyond film, so the Broncos will watch the first quarter for changes. On J.K. Dobbins, who played about four second-half snaps last week, Payton said he is a huge part of the offense and has been fantastic. He said the backfield is handled by who has the hot hand each week and that the staff is comfortable with the rotation. He admitted that rotating three backs is more challenging than two. He praised rookie running back Jonah Coleman's pass protection, versatility and ball skills, and said the tape and advanced protection plans gave the staff confidence in him as a third-down back. He said left tackle Garett Bolles' level of play lets the offense skip chips and nudges and trust him one-on-one. He also said the defense's pressure matters more than raw sack totals because pressure can produce interceptions, and he downplayed Bo Nix's slow starts. Payton said the team is playing better and is not looking to sell at the trade deadline, and he noted the new challenge of an East Coast early kickoff in Charlotte.

title: Campbell on Week 9 matchup
headline: No fantasy-relevant roster news: Campbell gave a positive update on LB Jack Campbell's medical situation and focused on preparing for Miami, with no injury, role or usage news on skill players.
summary: Campbell opened by saying the team is thankful for the positive news on Jack Campbell, whose own and his family's statements were encouraging. He said the linebacker's status has been improving every eight to ten hours. He then turned to Miami, which he called a young, hungry, hard-playing team that has gotten better over four weeks, with every game decided by one score. He praised the Dolphins' defense, mentioning Zach Sieler as the anchor, the linebackers, and a versatile nickel corner. On offense he highlighted an athletic line, a versatile scheme with plenty of motion, screens and gadgets, and a big, fast back in Gordon who is dangerous when he hits a crease with speed. He also complimented receiver Malik Washington, who plays slot and outside and returns punts. Campbell credited the medical and training staff for their care of Jack, said players are using the counseling resources available, and said the best way to honor Jack is to be locked in for the game. He also noted his respect for Steve Ross, who gave him his first head coaching shot in Miami.
